content:
The image shows cross-sectioned soybean stems. Key observations:

- **Affected part**: Stem (longitudinal cross-sections)
- **Color**: The internal pith/vascular tissue shows dark brown to reddish-brown discoloration
- **Pattern**: The discoloration is uniform and extends along the length of the stem interior, while the outer cortex remains lighter/green
- **Texture**: The browning appears in the pith area specifically

The pattern of **internal brown stem discoloration** with the outer tissue appearing relatively normal is characteristic of **Brown Stem Rot** (caused by *Cadophora gregata*). This disease is known for its hallmark brown discoloration of the pith and vascular tissue in the stem interior, visible when stems are split lengthwise. The contrast between the dark brown internal pith and the lighter outer tissue is the defining diagnostic feature shown here.

This is distinct from Sudden Death Syndrome (which shows foliar symptoms more), Phytophthora (which shows a soft dark rot often from the soil line), and Fusarium (which typically shows a red-pink discoloration in roots/lower stem).
